messages:
Maria: FYI we pushed Sentinel-3B q4f16 to canary last night and seeing punctuation spam in some chat sessions. lots of '!!!' and commas showing up mid-sentence.
Raj: ugh. can you paste an example? is this across prompts or specific ones?
Maria: short prompts. repro with: 'Summarize this article in one sentence.' -> output: 'Clear win,,,!!!'
Sam: interesting — looks like top-k selection might be hitting ties after logits quantization. did we run the top-k tie-breaker fix?
Priya: we didn't apply the deterministic tie-breaker change for q4 on this model because of the different kernel paths. thought it was low-risk.
Len: can we dump raw logits for the offending tokens? quick check: run with --logit-dump and compare fp16 vs q4.
Maria: ran that already, uploaded small dump: link to S3 (s3://redwood-debug/sentinel3b/q4/logits-dump-2429.tar.gz)
Raj: looked at dump — multiple tokens have identical rounded logits after quant. e.g. token ids [44, 67, 102] all 1.23e-2 after quantization step. topk=5 then chooses by position and our current shuffle leads to punctuation bias.
Sam: that explains punctuation clusters. if punctuation tokens sit earlier in vocab order they win ties. :facepalm:
Len: quick mitigation: enable deterministic tie-breaker that uses original fp32 logit ordering before rounding, or add tiny noise based on attention ctx id. which is easier to roll?
Priya: deterministic tie-breaker should be straightforward in runtime — use (logit, token_id) lexicographic compare where tie prefers higher fp32 logit. but we need fp32 reference; we only have quantized weights at runtime for q4.
Raj: alternative is to add epsilon from a stable hash(token_id, step) * 1e-6 to break exact ties. cheap and works inside quant path.
Maria: can we ship a hotfix to canary and run 1k chat requests? ops, can you schedule a canary redeploy? @Oncall-bot
Oncall-bot: @Maria scheduled canary redeploy to pool sentinel-canary-03 for 2429976600 UTC.
Sam: I'll push a patch that adds hashed epsilon tie-breaker in generation sampling. small diff:
```
# sampling.py
logits += (stable_hash(token_id) % 1000) * 1e-9
```
Priya: please also run evals against LM-evals prompt suite and the internal punctuation-sensitive tests. add metric: punctuation-rate and repetition-rate.
Len: note: this only surfaced after q4 quant for this arch because q8/q16 preserved fp granularity. worth adding a quantization regression check into onboarding checklist.
Maria: agreed. action items: 1) Sam push patch to canary (in flight). 2) Ops redeploy at 2429976600. 3) Priya run eval suite and attach report. 4) Raj compare logits fp16 vs q4 and post diff summary. 5) add gating test to onboarding checklist.
Raj: initial fp16 vs q4 summary: mean logit diff small but tie count up ~0.6% -> correlated with punctuation tokens. attaching quick table in the PR.
Sam: patch deployed to canary, sampling epsilon on. canary run started.
CI-bot: Canary health checks: 120/120 OK for infra, but application-level alerts: 2 regressions reported (punctuation-rate down from 12%->1.5% after patch).
Maria: preliminary looks good. can we keep canary running for another 2 hours and roll to dedicated if metrics stable?
Priya: running full evals now. ETA 35m. will share artifacts.
Len: follow-up: add a quantization checklist item: - compare token-order tie frequency across quant configs - run 10k short-prompt chat sample - add punctuation-sensitive metric - gate on tie-frequency threshold.
Raj: noted. I'll open onboarding ticket to update docs and add the test harness.
Maria: thanks all. closing for now but will follow results from Priya. :thumbsup:
